lat4-constitution3-en: Are all heresies that rise against the holy, orthodox, and Catholic faith to be excommunicated and anathematized, and heretics condemned under whatever names they may be known?
lat4-constitution4-en: May Greeks returning to obedience of the Apostolic See retain their customs and rites insofar as God's interests allow, while practices dangerous to souls or derogatory to ecclesiastical propriety are refused?
lat4-constitution5-en: After the Roman Church's pre-eminence as mother and mistress of the faithful, do the patriarchal sees rank Constantinople first, Alexandria second, Antioch third, and Jerusalem fourth, each bishop receiving the pallium from the Roman pontiff?
lat4-constitution6-en: Must metropolitans hold annual provincial synods with their suffragans to correct abuses, reform morals—especially of the clergy—and enforce the canons?
lat4-constitution7-en: Must prelates make a prudent, earnest effort to correct excesses and reform the morals of their subjects, especially the clergy, without custom or appeal blocking that duty unless they exceed due form?
lat4-constitution8-en: May a prelate inquire into and punish the excesses of subjects, including clerics, when those excesses come to the ears of the superior, as Scripture and the canons require?
lat4-constitution9-en: Where people of different languages share one faith but various rites, must bishops provide suitable men to celebrate the offices, administer the sacraments, and instruct them, while forbidding more than one bishop in the same city or diocese?
lat4-constitution10-en: Because the word of God is necessary food for Christian souls, must bishops provide suitable men powerful in work and word to exercise the office of preaching in their place when they cannot?
lat4-constitution11-en: Must every cathedral, and other churches with sufficient means, appoint a competent master to instruct gratis the clerics of that church and other poor students?
lat4-constitution12-en: In every ecclesiastical province, must abbots and priors without abbots hold a general chapter every three years, saving the rights of diocesan ordinaries?
lat4-constitution13-en: Is anyone forbidden in the future to found a new religious order, so that those wishing to enter religious life must choose an already approved order or rule?
lat4-constitution14-en: Must clerics, especially those in sacred orders, live chastely and virtuously, and is incontinence to be punished according to the canonical statutes in proportion to the gravity of the sin?
lat4-constitution15-en: Must all clerics carefully abstain from drunkenness and competitive drinking, and are hunting and fowling forbidden to them?
lat4-constitution16-en: Are clerics forbidden to hold secular offices, engage in dishonest pursuits, attend theatrical shows, visit taverns except when traveling, play games of chance, or wear superfluous or unbecoming attire?
lat4-constitution17-en: Must clerics and prelates celebrate the diurnal and nocturnal offices diligently and devoutly, rather than wasting the night in banqueting and neglecting Mass and the choir?
lat4-constitution18-en: May any cleric pronounce or execute a death sentence, be present at its execution, write letters for it, judge cases of bloodshed, practice cutting or burning surgery, or bless judicial ordeals?
lat4-constitution19-en: Must churches be kept as the house of God rather than storehouses for household goods, and be kept clean with decent vessels, vestments, palls, and corporals?
lat4-constitution20-en: Must the chrism and the Eucharist in all churches be kept in properly locked and protected places so they cannot be reached for impious or blasphemous purposes?
lat4-constitution21-en: Must all the faithful of both sexes, after the age of discretion, confess all their sins at least once a year to their own priest and receive the Eucharist at least at Easter, unless advised to abstain for a time?
lat4-constitution22-en: When physicians of the body are called to the sick, must they first admonish them to call for the physician of souls, so that spiritual health may be restored before bodily medicine is applied?
lat4-constitution23-en: Must a cathedral or regular church not remain without a bishop for more than three months, with the right of appointment devolving on the next superior if electors fail to elect in time?
lat4-constitution24-en: When an election is held with those present who ought and can attend, must the choice proceed by secret scrutiny of votes, by entrusted electors, or by absolute unanimity, other forms being invalid?
lat4-constitution25-en: Does one who consents to his own election through abusive secular intervention contrary to canonical liberty lose what he gained and become ineligible without dispensation?
lat4-constitution26-en: Before confirming an election for the guidance of souls, must the confirming authority carefully investigate the election and the elect, punishing both an unworthy promotee and a negligent confirmer?
lat4-constitution27-en: Must bishops diligently prepare and instruct those to be ordained priests in the divine offices and proper administration of the sacraments, rather than ordaining the ignorant and unformed?
lat4-constitution28-en: Are those who urgently seek permission to resign and then neglect to do so to be compelled to resign?
lat4-constitution29-en: Is anyone who accepts a second benefice with cure of souls after already holding such a benefice ipso jure deprived of the first, and of the second if he tries to retain both?
lat4-constitution30-en: Must bishops reject unworthy candidates for ecclesiastical benefices and choose suitable ones, with provincial synods investigating and suspending those who persist in unworthy collations?
lat4-constitution31-en: Are the sons of canons, especially illegitimate ones, forbidden to be made canons in the same secular churches where their fathers serve, such appointments being invalid?
lat4-constitution32-en: Must parish priests receive a sufficient portion of the revenues for decent subsistence, so that no custom of patrons or others may leave them with only a meager share of the tithes?
lat4-constitution33-en: May procurations due by reason of visitation be demanded, except in manifest urgent necessity, only when the visitor personally conducts the visitation and observes the limits on accompanying persons?
lat4-constitution34-en: Are prelates forbidden to extort from their subjects more for procurations than they hand over to papal legates and others, having to restore what was taken and give an equal amount to the poor?
lat4-constitution35-en: When someone sues before a competent judge, must he continue before that judge of first instance and not appeal without good reason before sentence is pronounced?
lat4-constitution36-en: May a judge proceed with the principal cause despite an appeal from an oppressive interlocutory sentence or threat, so that trifling circumstances do not delay the case?
lat4-constitution37-en: May anyone, by Apostolic letters, summon another before a judge more than two days distant from his diocese without both parties' consent or express mention of this restriction?
lat4-constitution38-en: In ordinary and extraordinary inquiries, must the judge employ a public person or two competent men to write down all acts of the proceedings so falsity may not prevail over truth?
lat4-constitution39-en: If someone knowingly accepts goods taken by a thief, becoming a participant in the theft, must the one robbed be assisted to obtain restitution from that possessor?
lat4-constitution40-en: If a plaintiff awarded possession for the opponent's contumacy cannot obtain it for a year through violence or deceit, does he still become the true owner, and may ecclesiastical decisions not be referred to lay arbitration?
lat4-constitution41-en: Is no prescription, whether canonical or civil, valid unless it rests on good faith, so that the holder must never knowingly possess what belongs to another?
lat4-constitution42-en: Must clerics abstain from arrogating lay rights under the pretext of ecclesiastical liberty, remaining content with approved laws and customs so that Caesar's things are rendered to Caesar and God's to God?
lat4-constitution43-en: May secular princes compel ecclesiastical persons under no temporal obligation to them to take an oath of fidelity?
lat4-constitution44-en: Have laymen, even pious ones, no power to dispose of ecclesiastical properties, and are laws attacking the immunity of Church goods, fiefs, jurisdictions, and mortuaries invalid?
lat4-constitution45-en: May patrons, advocates, and vicegerents of churches extend their jurisdiction beyond what the law permits in providing pastors or administering ecclesiastical goods?
lat4-constitution46-en: Are magistrates and rulers forbidden under anathema to oppress churches with taxes and exactions, except when bishop and clergy freely decide aid is needed and first consult the Roman pontiff?
lat4-constitution47-en: May a sentence of excommunication be promulgated against anyone without previous warning in the presence of suitable persons, or without a just and reasonable cause?
lat4-constitution48-en: If someone warned of excommunication claims suspicion of the judge, must that suspicion be examined through jointly chosen arbiters so that deceitful refusal or appeal cannot block the inquiry?
lat4-constitution49-en: Is anyone forbidden, from mere greed, to bind or absolve by excommunication especially for pecuniary gain, and must unjustly extorted money be restored with compensation for injury?
lat4-constitution50-en: Are marriages formerly barred in the second and third degrees of affinity, and certain related unions after second marriages, now permitted, with the prohibition not extending beyond the fourth degree?
lat4-constitution51-en: Must marriages be publicly announced in the churches by priests during a fixed time so impediments may be known, and are clandestine marriages absolutely forbidden?
lat4-constitution52-en: In reckoning degrees of consanguinity and affinity within the fourth degree, may hearsay witnesses be received only if they are reputable persons who learned from at least two reliable predecessors before the dispute arose?
lat4-constitution53-en: Must landowners who entrust cultivation to people unaccustomed to paying tithes still pay the churches the tithes in full, and must all tithes due by divine law or approved custom be paid?
lat4-constitution54-en: Does the payment of tithes, by the prerogative of general dominion, precede taxes and other expenses, so that one may not deduct such costs first in order to escape tithes?
lat4-constitution55-en: Must Cistercians pay tithes to the churches formerly entitled to them from lands they acquire, even if cultivated by their own hands or at their own expense, unless another arrangement is made?
lat4-constitution56-en: Are contracts by which clerics leasing houses or granting fiefs divert tenants' tithes and burial rights away from parochial churches condemned, with anything so received to be restored?
lat4-constitution57-en: Do privileges granting religious burial of their brethren during interdict apply only to true confrères not nominally excommunicated or interdicted, lest such privileges be abused?
lat4-constitution58-en: When a territory is under interdict, may bishops who did not cause it sometimes celebrate the divine offices with closed doors, in a low voice, and without bells, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted?
lat4-constitution59-en: May a religious go security for anyone or borrow beyond an amount fixed by common agreement without permission of the abbot and the greater part of the chapter?
lat4-constitution60-en: Are abbots forbidden to overreach into episcopal matters such as deciding matrimonial cases, imposing public penances, or granting letters of indulgence without special concession?
lat4-constitution61-en: Must regulars present to the bishop priests for churches not belonging to them pleno jure, so those priests answer to the bishop in the cure of souls and may not be removed without episcopal approval?
lat4-constitution62-en: May old relics be exhibited outside a vessel or exposed for sale, and may new relics be publicly venerated without approval of the Roman pontiff?
lat4-constitution63-en: Is demanding or extorting payment for consecrating bishops, blessing abbots, or ordaining clerics condemned as simoniacal corruption, sharing the condemnation of Gehazi and Simon?
lat4-constitution64-en: Is receiving nuns into a community for a price forbidden as simony, with both the one receiving and the one received to be removed to a stricter monastery to do penance?
lat4-constitution65-en: May bishops place vacant churches under interdict until money is paid for appointments, or exact gifts when someone enters a monastery or seeks burial among religious?
lat4-constitution66-en: Must the sacraments be administered freely without extorting money for burials, nuptial blessings, and similar things, while pious customs of free offerings are preserved?
lat4-constitution67-en: If Jews extort oppressive and immoderate interest from Christians, must commercial partnership with them be denied until suitable satisfaction is made, and princes strive to hinder such excesses?
lat4-constitution68-en: Must Jews and Saracens of both sexes in every Christian province be distinguished from others by the character of their dress at all times?
lat4-constitution69-en: Are Jews forbidden to be preferred to public offices over Christians, and must those who commit such offices to them be restrained by the provincial synod?
lat4-constitution70-en: Must those who voluntarily receive baptism be restrained by prelates from observing remnants of their former rite, so that they may perfectly put on the new life of the Christian religion?
lat4-ad-liberandam-en: Are those who have taken the cross to liberate the Holy Land to hold themselves prepared to assemble in the Kingdom of Sicily by June 1 of the appointed year to receive the Apostolic blessing?
con2-canon1-en: Is the nature or essence of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost one, with one force and power, a consubstantial Trinity and one Godhead worshipped in three Persons?
con2-canon2-en: Does the Word of God have two nativities—one from eternity of the Father without time or body, and another in these last days, made flesh of the holy and glorious Mary, Mother of God and ever-virgin?
con2-canon3-en: Is our Lord Jesus Christ one and the same Person—the Word of God incarnate—so that his miracles and the sufferings he endured in the flesh belong to the same Person, not to another Christ?
con2-canon4-en: Is the union of God the Word with flesh animated by a reasonable and living soul a true hypostatic union, not merely according to grace, energy, dignity, honor, authority, relation, or good pleasure?
con2-canon6-en: Is the holy, glorious, and ever-virgin Mary exactly and truly the Mother of God, because God the Word begotten of the Father before all ages was in these last days made flesh and born of her?
con2-canon7-en: When we say Christ is in two natures, do we mean an unconfused hypostatic union in which each nature remains what it was, not a division of the one Lord Jesus into separate parties?
con2-canon8-en: Does confessing two natures, or the one nature of God the Word made flesh, mean a hypostatic union of Godhead and humanity in one Christ, without mixture or confusion of the natures?
con2-canon9-en: Is Christ to be venerated by one adoration as God the Word made man together with his flesh, not by two separate adorations of the Word and of the man, nor by collapsing the natures into one mixed essence?
con2-canon10-en: Is our Lord Jesus Christ who was crucified in the flesh true God, the Lord of Glory, and one of the Holy Trinity?
con2-canon11-en: Must Arius, Eunomius, Macedonius, Apollinaris, Nestorius, Eutyches, Origen, and other heretics already condemned by the Church and the four holy Synods, together with their writings and followers, be anathematized?
con2-canon12-en: Must the teachings of Theodore of Mopsuestia—that the Word of God is one person and Christ another mere man who progressed into sonship—be rejected rather than defended?
con2-canon13-en: Must Theodoret's writings against the true faith, the Synod of Ephesus, and St. Cyril's Twelve Anathemas, and those who hold such opinions, be anathematized rather than defended?
con2-canon14-en: Must the letter said to be of Ibas to Maris the Persian—denying that the Word of God was made man of Mary the Mother of God, and attacking Cyril and Ephesus—be rejected rather than defended?
con2-sentence-en: Must the Church condemn and anathematize the Three Chapters—the impious Theodore of Mopsuestia and his writings, the impious writings of Theodoret, and the letter said to be of Ibas—together with their defenders?
lyo2-zelus-fidei-p1-en: Ought zeal for the faith, fervent devotion, and compassionate love to rouse Christians to rise in defense of the Holy Land consecrated by Christ's blood and attacked by the ungodly?
lyo2-zelus-fidei-p2-en: Must the pope, cardinals, and all ecclesiastical persons of whatever rank pay for six years a tenth of their ecclesiastical revenues for the aid of the Holy Land?
lyo2-zelus-fidei-p3-en: Are corsairs and pirates who impede travelers to the Holy Land, and Christians who sell arms, iron, timber, or ships to the Saracens for use against Christians, bound by excommunication and anathema?
lyo2-zelus-fidei-p4-en: May the great throng of prelates assembled for so sacred a council be allowed to depart when continuing presence becomes burdensome and their absence would harm their churches?
lyo2-constitution3-en: When opponents appeal against an election, postulation, or provision, must they state in a public document every objection they intend to raise against the form or the persons?
lyo2-constitution4-en: May anyone, before confirmation of his election, administer the office or interfere in its spiritual or temporal affairs under pretext of management, procuratorship, or any similar disguise?
lyo2-constitution5-en: After an election, must electors promptly inform the elect and ask his consent, and is the elect deprived of his right if he delays consent beyond a month from being informed?
lyo2-constitution6-en: Are those who knowingly vote for an unworthy candidate deprived of the power of electing only if they so persist that the election depends on their votes?
lyo2-constitution7-en: After voting for or consenting to an elect, may one oppose him concerning the election only for reasons later discovered or previously hidden vices of which he was probably ignorant, sworn under oath?
lyo2-constitution8-en: If after two scrutinies one part of the electors is more than double the other, is the minority barred from imputing lack of zeal, merit, or authority to the majority or their candidate, save for objections that nullify the election by law?
lyo2-constitution9-en: May an evidently frivolous extrajudicial appeal in episcopal or higher elections go before the apostolic see, or must only appeals from a credible and potentially legitimate motive be brought there?
lyo2-constitution15-en: Are those who knowingly ordain clerics of another diocese without the superior's permission suspended for a year from conferring orders?
lyo2-constitution19-en: Must every advocate in the ecclesiastical forum swear on the Gospels to defend only what they judge true and just for their clients, and to withdraw when they find the cause unjust?
lyo2-constitution24-en: Must visitors who exact or accept money for procurations, accept gifts, or take procurations without making the visitation restore double of what they received?
lyo2-constitution29-en: Is an admonition before major excommunication for communicating with the excommunicated canonical only if it names the persons admonished, with fitting intervals between admonitions unless urgency requires otherwise?
lyo2-constitution30-en: Does the benefit of provisional absolution apply to cities, villages, or other places against which a general interdict has been promulgated?
lyo2-constitution2-en: When the Roman see is vacant, must the cardinals follow strengthened procedures for electing the Roman pontiff so that a long and dangerous vacancy of the Apostolic See may be avoided?
lyo2-constitution10-en: If an elect is objected to for clear lack of knowledge or another obvious personal defect, must a fixed order of discussion and proof be observed in examining that charge?
lyo2-constitution11-en: Are those who oppress electors for refusing to elect a demanded candidate, or oppress the elect himself, to be restrained for such coercion?
lyo2-constitution12-en: May anyone usurp royal privileges, custody, or the title of advocate or defender over churches and monasteries and take possession of their property?
lyo2-constitution16-en: Are bigamists deprived of any clerical privilege and handed over to secular law, and forbidden under anathema to wear the tonsure or clerical dress?
lyo2-constitution17-en: Must canons who wish to suspend divine worship first express their reasons in an authenticated form before taking steps to suspend celebration?
lyo2-constitution20-en: Is any absolution from excommunication, suspension, or interdict that has been extorted by force or fear annulled?
lyo2-constitution21-en: Are dignities and benefices that become vacant in the Roman curia reserved to conferral by the Roman pontiff, as modified by this constitution?
lyo2-constitution22-en: May a prelate subject the churches entrusted to him, their immovable property, or rights to lay people without the consent of his chapter and special leave of the apostolic see?
lyo2-constitution25-en: Must churches be entered humbly and devoutly, with calm behavior inside that is pleasing to God and brings peace to those present?
lyo2-constitution26-en: Must the Lateran constitution against usurers be inviolably observed, closing up the abyss of usury that devours souls and swallows property?
lyo2-constitution27-en: Is ecclesiastical burial to be refused to notorious usurers until full restitution of usurious gains has been made as far as their means allow, even if their wills order restitution?
lyo2-constitution28-en: Are reprisals that burden some people in place of others forbidden as oppressive and contrary to law and natural equity?
lyo2-constitution31-en: Is anyone who, because of a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict, gives leave to kill, capture, or molest others in person or goods subject to grave penalty?
lyo2-constitution1-en: Does the Holy Spirit proceed eternally from the Father and the Son as from one principle and by one spiration, not as from two principles or by two spirations?
lyo2-constitution23-en: Is anyone forbidden to found a new order or form of religious life, and are unconfirmed mendicant forms founded after the earlier council's prohibition suppressed?
lyo2-constitution13-en: May anyone be appointed parish priest who is under twenty-five or not approved as to knowledge and morals, and must such a priest be ordained within the time the law requires?
lyo2-constitution14-en: May a parish church be given in commendam to anyone under lawful age or not ordained priest, and may a commendatory hold more than one parish church without evident need or advantage?
lyo2-constitution18-en: Must local ordinaries compel subjects who claim to hold several dignities or churches with cure of souls to produce the dispensations by which they assert they hold them canonically?
nic2-canon1-en: Must the sacred canons and canonical constitutions be observed in all things as the pattern for those who have received the sacerdotal dignity?
nic2-canon2-en: Must one who is to be ordained a bishop be steadfastly resolved to observe the canons, or else not be ordained?
nic2-canon3-en: Is every election of a bishop, presbyter, or deacon made by princes null, so that it does not pertain to princes to choose a bishop?
nic2-canon4-en: Must bishops abstain from all receiving of gifts, administering the Church's goods as in the sight of God rather than coveting anyone's silver or gold?
nic2-canon5-en: Are those who cast contumely upon clerics because they were ordained without bringing a gift to be punished with a fine?
nic2-canon6-en: Must a local synod of bishops be held in each province at the appointed time for canonical inquiries?
nic2-canon7-en: If churches were consecrated without any deposit of the relics of the saints, must that defect be made good?
nic2-canon8-en: Ought Hebrews to be received into the Church only when converted in sincerity of heart, not while feigning conversion and secretly denying Christ?
nic2-canon9-en: Must books containing the heresy of the traducers of the Christians and false writings against the venerable images be delivered up and not hidden?
nic2-canon10-en: May a cleric leave his own diocese and go into another without the knowledge of his bishop?
nic2-canon11-en: Ought œconomi to be appointed in episcopal palaces and in monasteries, as the divine canons require in each church?
nic2-canon12-en: May a bishop or hegumenos alienate farm lands of the bishopric or monastery into the hands of secular princes or other persons?
nic2-canon13-en: Are those who turn monasteries or bishops' palaces into public houses worthy of deposition or excommunication unless they restore them to sacred use?
nic2-canon14-en: May anyone without ordination read in the ambo during the synaxis, or may youths with only the tonsure do so contrary to the canons?
nic2-canon15-en: May a clergyman be set over two churches, as if one could serve two masters for filthy lucre?
nic2-canon16-en: Does costly, showy apparel or anointing with perfumes ill become those in holy orders, and ought bishops and clerics who so array themselves to correct themselves?
nic2-canon17-en: May anyone begin building an oratory or monastery who lacks the means to finish it, or must the local bishop forbid such unfinished undertakings?
nic2-canon18-en: Ought women to live in bishops' houses or in monasteries of men, or must those who retain women there for service be rebuked and, if unrepentant, deposed?
nic2-canon19-en: Must the vows of those in holy orders and of monks and nuns be made without the exaction of gifts?
nic2-canon20-en: May any double monastery be erected from henceforth, and must existing double monasteries be ordered so as to remove the offense?
nic2-canon21-en: May a monk or nun leave the monastery to which he or she is attached and transfer to another as a full member?
nic2-canon22-en: When monks must eat with women, ought they to observe thanksgiving, abstemiousness, and discretion, doing all to the glory of God?
nic2-definition-en: Just as the figure of the precious Cross is set forth, must venerable and holy images of Christ, the Mother of God, the angels, and the saints be set forth in churches and given relative veneration, not the worship due to God alone?
lat2-canon1-en: If anyone has been ordained simoniacally, must he entirely forfeit the office he illicitly usurped?
lat2-canon2-en: If anyone acquires a prebend, priory, deanery, ecclesiastical honor, chrism, holy oil, or consecration of altars or churches through payment, is that simoniacal acquisition condemned?
lat2-canon3-en: May those excommunicated by their bishops be received by others, and is one who knowingly communicates with an excommunicated person before absolution liable to the same sentence?
lat2-canon4-en: Must bishops and clergy be pleasing to God and others in interior and exterior comportment, giving no offence by the excess, cut, or colour of their clothing?
lat2-canon5-en: Are the goods of deceased bishops not to be seized by anyone, but left freely at the disposal of the treasurer and clergy for the needs of the church and the poor?
lat2-canon6-en: Are those in the orders of subdeacon and above who take wives or concubines to be deprived of their position and ecclesiastical benefice?
lat2-canon7-en: May anyone hear the Masses of those known to have wives or concubines, and must the law of clerical continence be upheld?
lat2-canon8-en: If women religious attempt to marry, are they to be treated under the same discipline as clerics who violate continence?
lat2-canon9-en: May monks and canons regular, after receiving the habit and making profession, study civil law and medicine for temporal gain in disregard of their rule?
lat2-canon10-en: May lay people possess the tithes of churches that canonical authority assigned for religious purposes, even if received from bishops or kings?
lat2-canon11-en: Must priests, clerics, monks, pilgrims, merchants, and peasants, with their plough animals and sheep, be left in peace in their coming, going, and work on the land?
lat2-canon12-en: Must the truce of God be inviolably observed from sunset Wednesday to sunrise Monday, and in the seasons from Advent to Epiphany and from Quinquagesima to Easter?
lat2-canon13-en: Is the greed of usurers condemned, and are usurers to be severed from every comfort of the Church?
lat2-canon14-en: Are jousts and tournaments in which knights rashly risk death and danger to souls entirely forbidden?
lat2-canon15-en: Is anyone who lays violent hands on a cleric or monk subject to anathema, and may no bishop presume to absolve such a person lightly?
lat2-canon16-en: Since ecclesiastical honours depend on merit rather than blood, may anyone claim churches, prebends, or offices by hereditary right?
lat2-canon17-en: Are unions within the bounds of consanguinity entirely prohibited as incestuous behavior detested by the holy fathers and the Church of God?
lat2-canon18-en: Is the crime of incendiarism completely forbidden by the authority of God and the blessed apostles Peter and Paul?
lat2-canon19-en: If an archbishop or bishop relaxes the decree against incendiarism, must he make restitution for the loss and abstain from his episcopal office for a year?
lat2-canon20-en: Do kings and princes retain the power to dispense justice in consultation with the archbishops and bishops?
lat2-canon21-en: Must sons of priests be removed from the ministries of the sacred altar unless they are living religiously in monasteries or canonries?
lat2-canon22-en: Must bishops and priests refuse to allow souls to be deceived by false penance, in which some sins are disregarded while others are retained?
lat2-canon23-en: Are those who, simulating a kind of religiosity, hold condemned errors to be expelled from the Church as heretics, constrained by the secular powers, with their defenders under the same condemnation?
lat2-canon24-en: May any sale-price be demanded for chrism, holy oil, and burials?
lat2-canon25-en: If anyone receives provostships, prebends, or other ecclesiastical benefices from the hand of a lay person, must he be deprived of the benefice unworthily received?
lat2-canon26-en: Must the custom of women living as nuns without the rule of Benedict, Basil, or Augustine be abolished?
lat2-canon27-en: Are nuns forbidden to come together with canons or monks in choir for the singing of the office?
lat2-canon28-en: Since churches may not be left vacant more than three months, may the canons exclude religious men from the election of a bishop after the see falls vacant?
lat2-canon29-en: Is the murderous art of crossbowmen and archers forbidden under anathema to be employed against Christians and Catholics?
lat2-canon30-en: Are the ordinances enacted by Peter Leoni and other schismatics and heretics void and null?
aa-1-en: Does the laity have a proper and indispensable role in the mission of the Church, so that apostolic activity of the people of God is to be intensified?
aa-2-en: Was the Church founded to spread the kingdom of Christ throughout the earth for the glory of God the Father, enabling all to share in his saving redemption?
aa-3-en: Do the laity derive the right and duty to the apostolate from their union with Christ the head, through Baptism and Confirmation?
aa-4-en: Does the success of the lay apostolate depend upon the laity's living union with Christ, since he is the source and origin of the whole apostolate of the Church?
aa-5-en: Does Christ's redemptive work include renewal of the whole temporal order, so that the Church's mission brings both the message and grace of Christ and the perfection of the temporal order?
aa-6-en: Is the apostolate of the Church and of all its members primarily designed to manifest Christ's message by word and deed and to communicate his grace to the world?
aa-7-en: Is it God's plan that men work together to renew and constantly perfect the temporal order—the goods of life and the prosperity of the family, culture, economy, arts, professions, politics, and international relations?
aa-8-en: While every exercise of the apostolate should be motivated by charity, are certain works by their nature specially vivid expressions of that charity and signs of Christ's messianic mission?
aa-9-en: Do the laity carry out their manifold apostolate both in the Church and in the world, in fields such as church communities, the family, youth, the social milieu, and national and international affairs?
aa-10-en: As sharers in Christ's role as priest, prophet, and king, is the activity of the laity so necessary within Church communities that without it the apostolate of the pastors is often unable to achieve its full effectiveness?
aa-11-en: Since conjugal society is a great mystery in Christ and the Church, do married persons and families have a special apostolate as the beginning and basis of human society?
aa-12-en: Do young persons exert a very important influence in modern society, so that their apostolate among themselves and in the wider community is of great consequence?
aa-13-en: Is the effort to infuse a Christian spirit into the mentality, customs, laws, and structures of the community so much the duty and responsibility of the laity that it can never be properly performed by others?
aa-14-en: On the national and international levels, do the laity especially assist with their Christian wisdom, in loyalty to their country and faithful fulfillment of their civic duties?
aa-15-en: Can the laity engage in their apostolic activity either as individuals or together as members of various groups or associations?
aa-16-en: Is the individual apostolate, flowing from a truly Christian life, the origin and condition of the whole lay apostolate, even of the organized type, admitting of no substitute?
aa-17-en: In regions where the freedom of the Church is seriously infringed, is there an urgent need for the individual apostolate, with the laity doing what they can to take the place of priests?
aa-18-en: Although the faithful are called to the apostolate as individuals, should they remember that man is naturally social and that God has been pleased to unite those who believe in Christ in one people of God?
aa-19-en: Is there a great variety of associations in the apostolate, some with the broad apostolic purpose of the Church and others aiming to evangelize, sanctify, or infuse a Christian spirit into the temporal order?
aa-20-en: Have associations of the laity that maintain a closer union with the hierarchy and pursue the apostolic aims of the Church a distinctive place among the forms of the lay apostolate?
aa-21-en: Must all associations of the apostolate be given due appreciation, especially those which the hierarchy have praised, recommended, or ordered as responsive to the needs of time and place?
aa-22-en: Do lay people who devote themselves with professional experience, permanently or temporarily, to the service of associations and their works deserve special honor and commendation in the Church?
aa-23-en: Whether exercised individually or in organizations, should the lay apostolate be incorporated into the apostolate of the whole Church according to a right system of relationships?
aa-24-en: Should the hierarchy promote the apostolate of the laity, provide spiritual principles and support, direct it to the common good of the Church, and attend to the preservation of doctrine and order?
aa-25-en: Should bishops, pastors, and other priests keep in mind that the right and duty of this apostolate is common to all the faithful, clergy and laity, and that in the lay apostolate they work as brothers with the laity?
aa-26-en: In dioceses, insofar as possible, should there be councils that assist the apostolic work of the Church in evangelization, sanctification, charitable, social, and other spheres, with due cooperation of clergy and laity?
aa-27-en: Do the quasi-common heritage of the Gospel and the common duty of Christian witness recommend and frequently require the cooperation of Catholics with other Christians, as individuals and communities?
aa-28-en: Can the apostolate attain its maximum effectiveness only through a diversified and thorough formation demanded by the spiritual and doctrinal progress of the lay person and by the circumstances of things and persons?
aa-29-en: Since the laity share in their own way in the mission of the Church, is their apostolic formation specially characterized by the distinctively secular quality of the lay state and by its own form of the spiritual life?
